title: wonky Num Lock Behavior
author: Tmiv44
summary: A pair of Keyboard Manager remaps involving Num Lock and Shift+semicolon leaves different applications observing inconsistent Num Lock state.
next_action: Record physical and injected key events plus LED/state transitions across the named applications.

confidence.rationale: The app matrix is concrete, but the current event/state mismatch is unmeasured.

judgment.rationale: The report gives both mappings and identifies application classes with opposite results, making it suitable for a controlled current reproduction.
evidence: Num Lock is remapped to colon.
Left Windows+Shift+semicolon is remapped back to Num Lock.
Calculator and Explorer produce number-key behavior while Office and Chrome produce navigation-key behavior.
judgment.recommended_action: Record physical and injected key events plus LED/state transitions across the named applications.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report does not show whether the inconsistency comes from toggle-state injection, remap recursion, application input APIs, or stale state from an old release.

issue_context.summary: A pair of Keyboard Manager remaps involving Num Lock and Shift+semicolon leaves different applications observing inconsistent Num Lock state.
known_information: The issue was reported on 0.63.0 while PowerToys ran elevated.
The behavior varies by target application.
inferences: Applications may read Num Lock through different APIs, exposing a mismatch between injected key events and system toggle state.
issue_context.analysis: A maintainer can reproduce the exact mapping matrix and inspect current event/state handling without additional reporter input.
initial_investigation: Read the complete mapping configuration and application comparison.
Confirmed current Keyboard Manager still handles low-level key events and remap state in native code.

actions.label: Reproduce Num Lock state mismatch
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Compare remapped Num Lock behavior across applications
prerequisites: Keyboard with numeric keypad and Num Lock indicator if available
Calculator, File Explorer, browser, and Office-like editor
setup: Create the two remaps exactly as reported.
Record the initial Num Lock state.
steps: Trigger the remap that should produce Num Lock.
Test numeric keypad behavior in each application.
Record the physical LED, GetKeyState result, and injected key sequence.
Disable Keyboard Manager and repeat as a control.
reproduce.expected_result: All applications should observe one consistent Num Lock toggle state after the remapped shortcut.
